headline: High: Mentat can write and modify shared files by default, creating prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-error risks when paired with a content-writing agent that may supply untrusted text.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a content-writing prompt repository, so its outputs can contain untrusted instructions; Agent B reads files and writes diffs from selected files by default. The pair has a filesystem bridge via B, so prompt injection is plausible even though A itself is not runnable and no direct shared channel is documented.
conditions: IF Agent A content is copied into files that Agent B reads
IF Agent B treats file text as instructions during edit proposal generation
mitigations: Restrict Agent B to a dedicated workspace folder
Require manual review of any prompt-like text before B processes it
Use file allowlists for B input paths
Add a provenance note to copied prompt content
requires-engineering: add content-type tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B can read and write filesystem contents and sends requests to a configured model provider, while Agent A is a docs-only prompt source with no network egress. If sensitive source code is placed in the shared workspace, B can transmit it to a third-party API; A does not add a second leak path, but the pair still exposes data through B.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the workspace B reads
IF B forwards file contents to its configured model provider
mitigations: Keep secrets out of B's workspace
Use redaction before files are passed to B
Disable network access for B where possible
Limit B to non-sensitive repositories
requires-engineering: route B through a local model endpoint

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent B has unrestricted filesystem write and modify_git_state, with shared state via filesystem across instances. Agent A is a content-writing source that can supply edit material, so if both touch the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes and git-state conflicts are dangerous by default; no locking is documented.
conditions: IF Agent A-derived content is used to generate edits in the same repository
IF multiple Agent B instances or other writers touch the same filesystem tree
mitigations: Run only one writer per repo at a time
Separate worktrees per agent
Pause git automation during edits
Review diffs before commit
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B produces diff-based edit proposals and can act on files it reads; if it consumes Agent A's prompt content as authoritative guidance, errors can cascade into incorrect code changes. Agent A is not a verifier, so the pair lacks a built-in verification step for transferred instructions.
conditions: IF Agent A output is used as input to B without human verification
IF B applies diffs derived from that content to production code
mitigations: Require human approval of every diff
Compare proposed edits against source requirements
Use a second reviewer for generated changes
Keep Agent A outputs out of production workflows
requires-engineering: add automated validation before commit

E_compliance.rationale: Agent B touches source code and sends it to a configured model provider, which can create retention or residency concerns if regulated code is involved. Agent A is only a docs-only prompt repository and does not itself process regulated data, so the compliance risk is mainly on B; the pair has limited overlap.
conditions: IF regulated source code or secrets are placed in files B reads
IF the configured model provider retains or relocates that data
mitigations: Use a provider with suitable contractual terms
Exclude regulated repositories from B
Strip secrets before analysis
Document retention settings
requires-engineering: enforce residency controls in the model gateway
